value.name: leave hidden confession for Lucia
value.description: The narrator writes a posthumous note meant for Lucia, explaining that she will find it in the pincushion where hidden items have been kept for decades.
evidence: If you are reading this it is because I am gone and because someone has thought to look in the pincushion, which is a place I have hidden things in for forty years and which none of you, in all that time, has ever noticed. Lucia, it will be you.

value.name: reveal terminal illness uncertainty
value.description: The narrator states that it is February and that doctors and body give conflicting signals about how much time remains.
evidence: I am writing this in February.
I do not know how long I have.
The doctor says one thing and my body says another and I have stopped asking either of them to be precise.

value.name: explain will change in own voice
value.description: The narrator says the letter exists to explain a deliberate legal decision personally rather than through a lawyer.
evidence: I am writing this because I have done a thing I want to explain in my own voice rather than in the voice of a lawyer.

value.name: sign will amendment
value.description: On February 11, the narrator visits Mr. Halloran and signs an amendment to the will.
evidence: I went to Mr. Halloran on the eleventh of February and I signed an amendment.

value.name: bequeath house to three heirs
value.description: The amendment leaves the Mifflin Street house in equal thirds to the narrator's daughter, son, and Rosa Maldonado.
evidence: The amendment says that the house on Mifflin Street is to be left in equal thirds to my daughter, my son, and to Rosa Maldonado

value.name: recognize Rosa's long care
value.description: The narrator acknowledges that Rosa has lived in and cared for the house and for the narrator longer and more faithfully than the children have.
evidence: who has lived in it longer than either of my children and who has cared for it and for me with a constancy I have never properly thanked her for.

value.name: restrict house sale and buyout terms
value.description: The amendment prevents the house from being sold without unanimous agreement and gives any resident heir first chance to buy out the others.
evidence: The amendment further says that the house may not be sold without the agreement of all three of these heirs

if any one of them wishes to remain living in the house, the other two must offer that person the first opportunity to buy out their shares at a fair valuation, with terms that do not require the sale of the house to a stranger.

value.name: anticipate son's accusations
value.description: The narrator predicts that the son will accuse her of confusion and manipulation by Rosa and the sister.
evidence: I am writing this because I know what my son will say.
He will say I was confused.
He will say Rosa influenced me.
He will say his sister has been working on me.
